jobs.description_text: Cowboy Space Corporation's team has worked at places like SpaceX, Blue Origin, Stoke Space, Astranis and NASA. About the Role: As a Mechanisms Engineer, you will own a critical spacecraft mechanism subsystem from concept through flight. Depending on your background and team priorities, your assignment will be hold-down and release mechanisms (HDRMs), solar array deployment and drive systems, deployable structures (antennas, booms, radiators), or thermal/radiator articulation mechanisms. This is a hands-on role at the center of spacecraft hardware development. jobs.description_text: This ambitious mission demands extraordinary talent. jobs.title: Controls Software Engineer, Pointing & Tracking
jobs.description_text: The Role As a Controls Software Engineer on the Pointing & Tracking team, you will own the software control loop that keeps a laser precisely pointed between two moving platforms, both satellite-to-ground and satellite-to-satellite. You will use closed-loop feedback from onboard sensors to drive fine-pointing actuators in an embedded real-time environment. This is control-systems software, not general application development: the core of the job is translating control theory into a robust, working real-time implementation and taking dedicated ownership of a system that is central to our mission. Responsibilities - Own the pointing and tracking control loop from design through on-orbit operations - Design, implement, and tune closed-loop controllers that keep optical links precisely pointed between moving platforms - Translate control theory (e.g., state estimation, PID, state-space, optimal control methods) into real-time embedded software in Rust - Perform stability analysis, closed-loop tuning, and performance characterization of control algorithms - Build simulation and analysis tools to model, validate, and iterate on control system behavior - Support hardware integration and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing of the full sensing-to-actuation chain - Develop automated test frameworks to validate control performance across operating conditions - Collaborate with GNC, optics, avionics, and firmware teams to define interfaces and system-level pointing architecture - Investig

jobs.title: Open Application - US
jobs.description_text: -- Can't find the right fit but still want to work with us? Apply here -- DRYFT Ideas only change the world when you build them at scale. That’s what Dryft is here for. Dryft builds models that automate complex human decisions in manufacturing operations. We capture the knowledge of experienced operators across supply chain, production planning, engineering and more, simulate the consequences of their decisions, and use this understanding to help run their business. Our customers include some of the largest robotics, machine and component manufacturers in the world. We’re a small, talent-dense team with modest roots and a love for the physical world: cars, machines, planes. Our team includes graduates from Stanford, Berkeley, CDTM and TUM, winners of Stanford TreeHacks, recipients of Fulbright & Haniel scholarships, and people who have built everything from robots and race cars to software with millions of downloads. What matters more to us than credentials is how people work: humility, hard work, speed, kindness, deep customer care, and a willingness to take on problems others avoid. Working at Dryft is hard. You get unusual ownership early on, with real responsibility. But that’s also what makes it one of the biggest learning experiences of your life. We’re backed by founders and operators behind some of the most legendary tech companies of our time, Tier-1 U.S. venture firms, and board members of global industrial companies. ERPs ran the physical world for half a century.

jobs.description_text: THE OPPORTUNITY Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone. As a backend engineer, you'd play a critical role in our search architecture. We're pretty flexible on what projects people work on based on their skills and interests. Search quality is bounded by what we understand about a page. Before anything can be retrieved, something has to work out what the page actually says. We crawl the web continuously and cannot keep all of it, refresh all of it, or spend a GPU on all of it. Something has to decide which pages are worth indexing, which links are worth following, which pages say the same thing as pages we already have, what has gone stale, and what we should never have picked up. These decisions are worth more than most ranking work. The cheapest way to improve search is to stop indexing pages nobody should ever retrieve, and to start indexing the ones we are missing. Today they run on a mix of learned signals and thresholds someone picked. We are looking for a research engineer to own the signals behind those decisions, and the decisions themselves. jobs.title: Applied Engineer, Hardware
jobs.description_text: Job Summary Designing frontier AI hardware means solving electrical and mechanical problems together: schematics and board layouts, power delivery and signal integrity, packaging and cooling, manufacturing and assembly. Every decision changes the constraints on the next. Future breakthroughs will come from AI systems that can reason across these domains, operate engineering tools, run thousands of experiments, and learn which designs work in the physical world. You will build those systems. Your mandate is to build agents that take electrical and mechanical designs from requirements through verified, manufacturable outputs. These agents should create and modify CAD models, design schematics and PCB layouts, run simulations, diagnose failures, and iterate with our engineers, pushing the limits of how much of the design process AI can own end to end. Etched offers a uniquely tight research loop: chips, boards, racks, cooling systems, manufacturing, and dedicated in-office compute under one roof. By architecting and orchestrating agent loops, you will turn proprietary designs, simulation results, engineering decisions, and physical test data into systems that get better with every experiment—and ship the hardware they help design. jobs.title: Fleet Software Lead
jobs.description_text: Job Summary We’re hiring a Fleet Systems Lead to join our Supercomputing organization. This team builds the software that enables Etched to deploy inference clusters at gigawatt-scale. This role presents an opportunity to shape how frontier inference hardware is deployed, managed, and orchestrated for our customers. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing methods so frontier models can run with best-in-class throughput, latency, cost, and power efficiency for both prefill and decode workloads. Fleet Software enables deployments of these systems at scale through configuration management, safe software and firmware rollouts, and software recovery, while partnering with other engineering teams to drive product improvements as we ramp production at unprecedented speed. The team also builds the monitoring and analysis systems that connect signals across the rack. Engineers and their agents use this data to investigate failures, spot patterns and continually improve the performance and reliability of the inference fleet. We’re looking for a leader to drive technical direction while building the best team in the industry. Someone who has built infrastructure and owned it through real deployments in the field. This team’s work will shape how Etched scales to a computing platform that customers depend on at massive scale. Key Responsibilities - Lead and develop the Fleet Software team. jobs.description_text: Job Summary We’re hiring a Node Systems Lead to join our Supercomputing organization. This team builds the software that enables Etched to deploy inference clusters at gigawatt-scale. This role presents an opportunity to shape how frontier inference hardware is configured and managed for our customers. We co-design chips, racks, software, and manufacturing methods so frontier models can run with best-in-class throughput, latency, cost, and power efficiency for both prefill and decode workloads. Node Systems owns the software layer of each individual Etched node, from host software and system configuration to the interfaces between rack components. It tunes CPU scheduling, memory, networking, and host-to-accelerator communication so models get every bit of performance and reliability our hardware can deliver, then turns those gains into tested software and configurations that ship in every system. We’re looking for a leader who can set the technical direction and dive deep into difficult systems problems. Someone who has taken hardware from early bring up into production, can build the best team in the industry, and wants to stay close to architecture and code. The team’s work is central in enabling Etched to deploy inference clusters at massive scale. This hands-on role combines equipment maintenance with day-to-day process support to improve uptime, product quality, and manufacturing efficiency. You will work closely with Production, Process Engineering, and Quality to resolve equipment issues, support product changeovers and new product introductions, and prevent recurring failures. It runs across football, baseball, tennis, American football, ice hockey, cricket, basketball and rugby, on-premise, in the cloud and increasingly on edge devices, delivered by over 100 engineers in the Tracking and Automated Officiating value stream. You would be the person who decides how that is built. The role carries two hats. As Software Architect you own the software-level architectural design across tracking, auto-officiating and data delivery. As computer vision authority you lead the core domains: camera calibration, ball tracking, skeletal tracking, and the R&D that feeds them. It is a hands-on job. You set architecture for new tracking problems as they arrive, you safeguard the shared frameworks, and when a live delivery is at risk you are the escalation point who gets into the code. WHAT YOU WOULD OWN Architecture across the value stream. You are the lead architect for every tracking and auto-officiating product in T&AO. You set the initial architecture when a new tracking problem enters the business, run the Software Domain Owner model so shared libraries like calibration have named codeowners, and keep designs consistent across sports. jobs.title: Senior Full Stack Engineer
jobs.description_text: You'll build the interfaces people use to run H's agents: the H Platform https://hcompany.ai/h-platform, where teams deploy an agent, follow it live and replay what it did step by step, and HoloTab https://hcompany.ai/holotab, our Chrome extension that controls the browser on its user's behalf. The work is mostly front end, in React and TypeScript, with changes to the Python APIs behind it when a feature calls for them. H builds agents that use a computer the way a person does, in the browser and on the desktop. WHAT YOU'LL OWN How people watch, steer and replay an agent while it acts on a computer, which has few established patterns yet. You'll decide how a live run appears and plays back, how live data gets to the screen, how a feature splits between front end and API, and which components become shared standards. We'll judge the work by what ships to users, by front-end quality held in CI, and by whether people can follow and control what an agent did. WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING - Building the H Platform web app - Building and improving the HoloTab extension - Designing the live run view and replay - Changing the Python APIs behind a feature - Setting shared component patterns - Making long-running workflows easier for FDEs and customers to deploy and watch THE FIRST YEAR Within three months, a feature you built, API change included, is with users. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - London
jobs.description_text: ABOUT H: When we released Holo4 https://hcompany.ai/newsroom/holo4 on 28 September, we published every trajectory behind its public benchmark scores at trajectories.hcompany.ai http://trajectories.hcompany.ai. For OSWorld that's 369 desktop tasks, each run 3 times, with the steps, tokens and time of every attempt. This role builds and runs the evaluation framework that produces runs like these. H builds computer-use agents and the models behind them. Developers use them through a managed API https://hcompany.ai/newsroom/computer-use-agents-api, and our forward deployed engineers take them into enterprise workflows. WHAT THIS TEAM OWNS The evaluation framework: orchestration, runtimes and observability. Researchers and forward deployed engineers bring the benchmarks, across web apps, desktop applications and the command line. Your job is to make the framework that runs them reliable, fast and cheap, and to make adding a new one quick. Research uses the results to choose checkpoints and decide whether a model ships. Product and the forward deployed engineers use them to measure agents on customer workflows. It carries roughly 50 benchmarks now. That number should be between 100 and 200 soon, and the framework has to keep up. WHAT YOU'D BE DOING - Integration support for researchers and forward deployed engineers bringing in a benchmark, with a shorter path each time. - Setting the standard for how a benchmark enters the framework, and building the checks that enforce it. - Sche

jobs.title: Business Partner / Executive assistant to CEO
jobs.description_text: About H: H exists to push the boundaries of superintelligence with agentic AI. By automating complex, multi-step tasks typically performed by humans, AI agents will help unlock full human potential. H is hiring the world’s best AI talent, seeking those who are dedicated as much to building safely and responsibly as to advancing disruptive agentic capabilities. We promote a mindset of openness, learning, and collaboration, where everyone has something to contribute. About the role: We’re looking for an Executive Business Partner to work alongside our CEO as a strategic partner. You’ll decide where his time goes, prepare him for every important conversation and keep the company aligned with his priorities. You’ll be a senior member of the CEO Office, with the authority to decide which meetings, events and requests make it onto his agenda. Key Responsibilities: - Own the CEO’s agenda and priorities. You’ll decide which meetings, events and requests he takes on based on company priorities, and escalate only the hardest calls. - Triage inbound requests such as speaking invitations, events, and approaches from partners and investors, and put forward clear recommendations. - Brief the CEO before key meetings with the context, the objectives and the points he needs to land. - Act as the CEO’s point of contact for investors, partners and the leadership team, representing him with judgement and discretion. - Manage the CEO’s inbox and complex international travel so he can stay focused
